chunks.label: Monday to Thursday
chunks.rationale: Lets you name the first four days of the week.
chunks.interference: Getsu in getsuyoubi is the same moon word as -gatsu in month names.

chunks.label: Friday to Sunday
chunks.rationale: Finishes the week and lets you ask which day something is on.
chunks.interference: Nan'youbi asks the weekday; nannichi asks the date.

chunks.label: Three daily meals
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about breakfast, lunch and dinner.
chunks.interference: Ohiru means both noon and lunch.

chunks.label: Weekdays and days off
chunks.rationale: Lets you use the short day names and talk about workdays versus days off.
chunks.interference: Kyuujitsu (any day off) vs shukujitsu (public holiday).

chunks.label: January to June
chunks.rationale: Lets you name the first six months.

chunks.label: July to December
chunks.rationale: Lets you name the last six months.
chunks.interference: Shichigatsu (July) sounds close to ichigatsu (January); September is kugatsu, never kyuugatsu.

chunks.label: Asking and counting months
chunks.rationale: Lets you ask the month and say how many months something takes.

chunks.label: The 1st to 5th
chunks.rationale: Lets you say the first five dates and spans of two to five days.
chunks.interference: Tsuitachi is only the date; a day long is ichinichi.

chunks.label: The 6th to 10th
chunks.rationale: Lets you say the 6th to the 10th and spans of six to ten days.
chunks.interference: Youka (8th) vs yokka (4th); muika (6th) vs mikka (3rd).

chunks.label: Other dates
chunks.rationale: Lets you say any date in the month and ask what the date is.

chunks.label: Counting days
chunks.rationale: Lets you say how many days something lasts.

chunks.label: Parts of the day
chunks.rationale: Lets you place things in the morning, afternoon, daytime or early evening.
chunks.interference: Gozen and gogo go before the hour (gogo sanji), unlike English a.m. and p.m.

chunks.label: Night and late night
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about evenings and the small hours.
chunks.interference: Yonaka and shin'ya overlap; shin'ya sounds more official.

chunks.label: Nearby days and nights
chunks.rationale: Lets you point to last night, tonight, the other day and two days either side of today.
chunks.interference: Ototoi (day before yesterday) vs ototoshi (year before last).

chunks.label: Every morning, week, year
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe routines and how often things happen.
chunks.interference: Maitsuki and maitoshi have formal twins, maigetsu and mainen.

chunks.label: Further back and ahead
chunks.rationale: Lets you go two weeks or two years either way, or a day either side of an event.
chunks.interference: Zenjitsu and yokujitsu count from an event, not from today.

chunks.label: Formal meal words
chunks.rationale: Lets you follow dinner and breakfast talk at hotels and on menus.

drops.reason: Spelling variant of か月; the same -kagetsu counter.
